slides.title: prompts to build a workout + meal routine that fits your real week
slides.sub: Give it your schedule, budget and energy — it does the planning.
slides.voiceover: Here are five prompts that build a workout and meal plan around your real week.

slides.name: The Weekly Split
slides.sub: A workout plan built around the days you actually have.
slides.prompt: Build me a weekly workout plan using only the time I really have: [DAYS I CAN TRAIN], [MINUTES PER SESSION], [EQUIPMENT: HOME / GYM / NONE]. I'm at a [FITNESS LEVEL] level. Make it **SPECIFIC** (sets, reps, rest) and **REALISTIC** for a busy week, not an ideal one.
slides.tip: Give it your worst week, not your best one — the plan should still work when Tuesday gets eaten by a late meeting.
slides.voiceover: One. Give it your real days and time, not your ideal week.

slides.name: The One-List Shop
slides.sub: Every ingredient from your meals, combined into one trip.
slides.prompt: Take this week's meals: [LIST YOUR MEALS OR PASTE A PLAN]. Combine every ingredient into **ONE** grocery list, grouped by store aisle (produce, protein, pantry...), with quantities for [NUMBER OF PEOPLE]. The goal: no double trips, no guessing.
slides.tip: Paste it straight into your phone's notes app — grouped by aisle, it doubles as a map of the store.
slides.voiceover: Two. One prompt turns your meals into a single, sorted shopping list.

slides.name: Meals For Your Constraints
slides.sub: Dinner ideas that fit your diet, budget and time.
slides.prompt: Suggest 7 dinner ideas that fit [DIETARY CONSTRAINTS: e.g. vegetarian, no dairy], a weekly budget of [BUDGET], and under [MAX COOK TIME] minutes each. Prioritize meals that **REUSE** the same ingredients so nothing goes to waste.
slides.tip: Ask it to reuse the SAME 8-10 ingredients across all 7 meals — that's what actually keeps the grocery bill down.
slides.voiceover: Three. It builds meals around your diet, your budget, and how much you cook.

slides.name: The Progress Tracker
slides.sub: One simple table that shows if it's actually working.
slides.prompt: Build me a simple weekly tracker table for [WORKOUTS COMPLETED, WEIGHT OR MEASUREMENTS, ENERGY LEVEL 1-5]. Keep it to one table I can update in under a minute, and have it flag when a number hasn't **MOVED** in 2 weeks.
slides.tip: Update it on the same day every week — Sunday night works well — so the trend is actually comparable.
slides.voiceover: Four. A simple weekly table shows you if anything's actually moving.

slides.name: The Simplify Button
slides.sub: For when the plan gets too big to keep up with.
slides.prompt: My routine from the prompts above has gotten too complicated and I've skipped it [NUMBER] times this week. Cut it down to the **SMALLEST** version that still counts as progress, based on only [TIME OR DAYS I ACTUALLY HAVE] right now.
slides.tip: Run this the moment you notice you're avoiding the plan — before you quit it completely.
slides.voiceover: Five. Stuck? One prompt shrinks the plan back to what you'll actually do.

slides.title: Get more out of this pack
items: Run all 5 prompts in the same chat so it remembers your schedule, budget and level throughout.
Real days and real minutes beat 'sometime this week' — vague input gives vague plans.
Feed last week's tracker numbers back into prompt one to adjust the plan, not just repeat it.
slides.voiceover: Three habits that make these prompts actually stick week after week.
